ns1:channel.ns1:title: Nature
ns1:channel.ns1:description: Nature is the foremost international weekly scientific journal in the world and is the flagship journal for Nature Portfolio. It publishes the finest peer-reviewed research in all fields of science and technology on the basis of its originality, importance, interdisciplinary interest, timeliness, accessibility, elegance and surprising conclusions. Nature publishes landmark papers, award winning news, leading comment and expert opinion on important, topical scientific news and events that enable readers to share the latest discoveries in science and evolve the discussion amongst the global scientific community.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Genome accessibility reveals disease risk that gene expression misses
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03072-5

Most disease-associated genetic alterations do not affect the genes themselves, but instead change how strongly they are expressed, often by modifying genome accessibility. Gene expression and accessibility have now been analysed simultaneously in 10 million immune cells from 1,108 people, linking disease-associated changes in accessibility to gene expression.
ns1:item.dc:title: Genome accessibility reveals disease risk that gene expression misses

ns1:item.ns1:title: An early predecessor to mammals could swim, suckle and swallow
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03069-0

A fossil of an early ancestor of mammals from the Jurassic period reveals a mammal-like throat passage (pharynx) and throat bones (hyoids). It fills a gap in our knowledge about throat features in the animals from which modern mammals evolved their ability to swallow as adults and suckle milk as babies.
ns1:item.dc:title: An early predecessor to mammals could swim, suckle and swallow

ns1:item.ns1:title: How to control where semiconductor crystals start growing
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02934-2

Semiconductor crystals grow from tiny nuclei, but the position of these nuclei is difficult to control precisely and can affect the crystal’s properties. An approach using ‘etching flux’ has now been developed that constrains the position at which a nucleus forms, enabling spatially programmable growth of large single crystals of semiconducting material.
ns1:item.dc:title: How to control where semiconductor crystals start growing

ns1:item.ns1:title: Cryo-EM structure of a methanogen nitrogenase–PII protein supercomplex
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11116-z

Cryo-electron microscopy of a nitrogenase supercomplex from a methane-producing archaeon reveals a mechanism in which PII proteins drive assembly of such structures to regulate nitrogenase activity in response to nitrogen availability.

ns1:item.ns1:title: A Jurassic mammaliaform swimmer and transformation of the mammalian pharynx
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11107-0

A swimming and water-foraging mammaliaform, Megacauda sungei gen. et sp. nov., had a lifestyle analogous to the extant platypus, and was capable of mammal-like swallowing and suckling.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Human lung organoid modelling of tissue-resident antiviral T cell responses
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11114-1

Lung organoids containing endogenous resident immune cells show that SARS-CoV-2 infection elicits protective, tissue-resident memory T cell responses, demonstrating local recall immunity and providing a platform for the study of human tissue-resident antiviral defence.

ns1:item.ns1:title: A gut microbial odd-chain fatty acid alleviates atherosclerosis in mice
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11142-x

The administration of Bacteroides uniformis in mice can mitigate atherosclerosis via pentadecanoic acid, which directly inhibits HMG-CoA reductase to promote hepatic cholesterol clearance.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Observation of critical topological phase transition
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11067-5

Using an acoustic metamaterial platform, a critical topological phase transition is experimentally demonstrated establishing a hierarchical phase transition organization, in which topology shapes criticality beyond the conventional Landau–Ginzburg paradigm and standard topological phase transitions.

ns1:item.ns1:title: 5-oxoETE links redox control of epithelial damage detection and resilience
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11121-2

The DHRS7–OXER1 pathway links oxidative stress to immunity and tissue resilience by modulating 5-oxoETE via NADP+–NADPH, activating OXER1 to recruit antimicrobial cells and induce NUDIX enzymes that protect epithelial redox integrity.
